name: python-exam-grading-rubric
description: Grading rubric for the EXPANDED Python Engineering exam bank (coding and open-ended each 3x). Covers the three modalities (auto-scored MCQ, executed code, rubric-graded open-ended) and how each item's score feeds the adaptive test (CAT/IRT). Adapted from the Masar open-ended grading rubric.

applies_to.note: Expanded bank: MCQ kept as-is; coding and open-ended tripled to 30 each. Every coding and open item carries the 4-criterion 20-point rubric; MCQ are auto-scored.

mcq.method: Automatic. score = 1.0 if the selected option index == mcq.answer_index else 0.0.
mcq.misconception_capture: On a wrong answer, record mcq.misconceptions[selected_index] as the diagnosed misconception for reporting.

code.method: Execute the candidate's function against code.tests in a sandbox; score = sum(weight for passing tests) / sum(all weights). Optionally apply the 20-point rubric (functional_correctness 8, edge_case_handling 5, algorithm_choice 4, code_quality 3) for a richer human/LLM score.
code.reference: code.reference_solution passes all tests (verified at build time by execution).
code.unit_score: weighted fraction of tests passed, in [0,1]

open.method: Silent LLM grading against the 20-point rubric (technical_accuracy 8, completeness 5, reasoning_and_justification 4, clarity_and_communication 3).
open.pitfall_rule: Each item.open.common_pitfalls the answer commits caps technical_accuracy and is recorded.

difficulty_calibration.purpose: Item difficulty is real, not just labelled. Each item was written to an explicit target and independently re-rated; cat.b is assigned in well-separated bands so easy items are genuinely easier than hard ones in the IRT sense.

target_pass_rates.note: Difficulty is anchored to the fraction of professional Python developers expected to answer correctly (mcq.est_dev_pass_rate_pct records the estimate per item).

difficulty_calibration.verification: Every item was re-rated by an independent reviewer that did not see the intended difficulty; items off by more than one band were rewritten. Key technical claims were cross-checked against docs.python.org (see VERIFICATION.md).

guessability.purpose: MCQ items are built to resist guessing; a candidate with no Python knowledge should not beat 1-in-4 by surface features.
controls: Four individually-plausible distractors; no joke or throwaway options.
Correct option not distinguishable by length, specificity, grammar, or stem echo.
Independent reviewer flags any item a zero-knowledge taker could beat by pattern-matching; flagged items were rewritten.
guessability.encoded_in_cat_c: mcq.guess_resistance maps to cat.c (the IRT pseudo-guessing floor): high -> 0.06-0.12, medium -> 0.13-0.19, low -> 0.20-0.25. Code and open items are constructed-response, so cat.c = 0.0.

discrimination_levels.purpose: The discrimination label reflects the IRT slope cat.a — how sharply the item separates candidates. It is INDEPENDENT of difficulty.
discrimination_levels.field: mcq.discrimination / code.discrimination / open.discrimination; numeric slope is cat.a.
discrimination_levels.cat_use: Prefer higher-a items near the current theta for faster convergence; down-weight low-a items.

cat_integration.model: 3PL for MCQ (a, b, c), 2PL for code/open (c = 0.0). cat.b encodes difficulty, cat.a discrimination (independent of difficulty), cat.c the MCQ guessing floor.
cat_integration.response_scoring: Feed each item's unit_score to the theta update: MCQ is dichotomous (0/1); code and open are graded/partial-credit in [0,1].
cat_integration.dichotomous_fallback: If the engine needs binary for code/open, mark correct when unit_score >= 0.60 (aligned with the 'knows' boundary).
cat_integration.selection: The CAT engine picks the next item by Fisher information (a function of cat.a and the gap between theta and cat.b) at the current ability estimate.

guardrails.no_length_bias: For open items, reward substance matching expected_answer_points, not verbosity.
guardrails.penalise_fabrication: Confident-but-wrong specifics are scored as errors, never completeness.
guardrails.silent_grading: Never reveal reference answers, expected points, pitfalls, or scores to the candidate during the assessment.
